from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + x

    # Current best ratio p/q, starting from the first window of length k.
    p, q = prefix[k], k

    # Dinkelbach iteration: for ratio p/q, maximize sum(q*a_i - p) over
    # subarrays of length >= k. A positive maximum means a strictly better
    # average exists; the maximizing subarray gives the next ratio.
    while True:
        best_val = None
        best_i = best_j = -1
        min_val = None
        min_idx = -1
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            wi = q * prefix[i] - p * i
            if min_val is None or wi < min_val:
                min_val = wi
                min_idx = i
            wj = q * prefix[j] - p * j
            val = wj - min_val
            if best_val is None or val > best_val:
                best_val = val
                best_i = min_idx
                best_j = j
        if best_val <= 0:
            break
        p = prefix[best_j] - prefix[best_i]
        q = best_j - best_i

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
